summary: The equivalence and optimality conclusion are correct. For an arbitrary admissible measurable density, the induced fiber masses lie in [0,v] and their normalized average in the base cube can be integral only at a cube vertex; coordinatewise extremality then forces every positive fiber mass onto that single vertex fiber, so a <= v. Conversely, the constant density a/v on one vertex fiber is admissible for every 0 < a <= v, including a = v, and has barycenter (q,c_K). Accepted fact 725defc391f9d55d supplies a fiberwise density of mass W/2^n with integral-base barycenter for every eligible body, while this product body excludes every larger mass, so the universal factor 2^{-n} is exactly optimal at this interface.
